About: The Beam That Will Not Turn

Source

Topic
Static equilibrium of a rigid body — a light beam on two end supports carrying a sliding load.
Concept
Balancing the forces tells you the two supports carry the whole weight — but only balancing the torques tells you how they split it.
Audience
JEE / NCERT Class 11–12. Standard result named: law of the lever (moments about a support).
Misconception targeted
“The supports each take half.” They only do at the midpoint; a load over one support puts the entire weight on it.

Guided Inquiry

Predict — load at two-fifths of the span

A 10 kg load hangs at x = 2 m on a 5 m beam resting on two end supports. How is its weight shared between the LEFT and RIGHT supports?

Read the arrows

Look at the two blue and green arrows. Their combined length stays visibly constant as you drag the load — that's ΣF = 0. But their individual lengths TRADE — that's the torque condition doing work you can see.

Notice: it's the support closer to the load that grows taller. The lever arm from the far support is longer, so the far support gets a smaller share.

Slide to the midpoint

The load has been placed at x = 2.5 m — the two arrows equalise at exactly N_L = N_R = 49.05 N. This is the ONE position where “each takes half” is true.

Now slide the load all the way to x = 0 (over the left support). The right arrow vanishes; the left takes the whole 98.1 N. The share is fixed by geometry, not by fairness.

Verify — which condition sets the split?

Both readouts sit at zero at every position. What does that mean the split N_L : N_R is fixed by?

The lever arm is a perpendicular distance

The dashed line under the beam is the lever arm from the LEFT support to the load's line of action — a distance, not a position. Torque is force times PERPENDICULAR distance, and it's this length that appears in Στ = 0.

You now own the full simulation. Both conditions sit at zero because both are enforced — remove either and the beam either falls or turns.

The Physics

The Beam That Will Not Turn — Two Conditions, Not One · what this sim shows, the physics behind it, and every control

01

At a glance

A light beam rests on two end supports, A on the left and B on the right, 5 m apart. A load sits on the beam, and you can slide it along the span. Each support pushes up on the beam. The question is how much each one carries.

What you'll learn

  • What a beam at rest must satisfy about forces and torques.
  • How the load's position and mass enter the supports' forces.
  • Which of the two conditions decides how the weight is divided.
  • Why a lever arm is a perpendicular distance.
The beam, its two supports and the load. The ruler shows where the load sits.

What's on screen

  • Amber box: the load, sitting on the beam at position x.
  • Red arrow: the load's weight W, pointing down.
  • Blue arrow: the upward force NL at A. Green arrow: NR at B. All three arrows share one scale.
  • Dashed grey line: the lever arm from support A to the load.
See itStart with the load 2 m from A and a mass of 10 kg. Watch for: the red weight arrow, the dashed lever-arm line from A and the label lever arm = 2.00 m.

03

Force balance fixes only the total

The beam does not accelerate up or down, so the vertical forces cancel. The two supports must together hold up the load's weight:

ΣFy = 0 ⇒ NL + NR = W = mg
The sim uses g = 9.81 m/s², so 10 kg weighs 98.1 N.

This is one equation for two unknowns. Many splits add up to 98.1 N, for example 49.05 + 49.05 or 90 + 8.1, so force balance alone cannot say how the weight is shared. It does explain why the blue and green arrows always add up to the red one.

See itUse x = 3.5 m and m = 10 kg, then drag x. Watch for: the blue and green arrows together are as long as the red arrow, and ΣFy reads 0.00 N.
04

Torque balance about a support fixes the split

The beam also does not turn, so the torques cancel about any point. Choose support A. Its own force then has no lever arm and drops out. Only NR at the lever arm S and W at the lever arm x remain:

ΣτA = 0 ⇒ NR·S − W·x = 0
Torque is force times the perpendicular distance, so x is measured along the beam, square to the force.

Solving, NR = W·x/S and NL = W·(S − x)/S. The support nearer the load carries more. At x = 2 m the shares are 3/5 and 2/5.

x (m)01245
NL (N)98.178.558.919.60

See itPut the load at x = 2 m with m = 10 kg. Watch for: the blue arrow at A is taller than the green one at B, in the ratio 3 to 2.
See itPut the load at the midpoint, x = 2.5 m. Watch for: the blue and green arrows are equal in length, each half the red arrow.
05

The mass scales both forces and leaves the split alone

W = mg appears in both NL and NR, so the load's mass does not choose the split. It only sets the size of the forces. At x = 2 m the shares stay 60% and 40%, whatever m is. At 20 kg, W = 196.2 N and the supports carry 117.72 N and 78.48 N.

Only the position sets the split. The midpoint is the one place where "each takes half" is true. With the load right above a support, that support carries the whole weight and the other carries nothing.

Both readouts stay at zero everywhere, because the beam is in equilibrium at every position.

See itKeep x = 2 m and set m = 20 kg. Watch for: the red arrow twice as long as at 10 kg, and both blue and green arrows doubled, still 3 to 2.
See itSlide the load all the way left, to x = 0. Watch for: the blue arrow as long as the red arrow, and no green arrow at B.
06

Where it matters

  • Bridges and floors. A truck on a beam bridge loads the two abutments unequally, and the engineer finds each share by taking moments about one support.
  • Carrying a load together. Two people carrying a heavy pole share its weight unequally. The one nearer the load takes more.
  • Weighing with two scales. A plank on two scales with a load on top reads the same split, and the scales add up to the total weight.
  • Ladders and shelves. A shelf bracket or a ladder resting on two points is checked the same way: forces for the total, moments for the split.
07

Summary

In one line. A beam at rest needs both its forces and its torques to balance, and the two jobs are different.

Key points

  • ΣFy = 0 gives the total, NL + NR = mg.
  • Στ = 0 about a support gives the split, NR = mg·x/S and NL = mg·(S − x)/S.
  • The nearer support carries more, and the mass only scales both.
  • A lever arm is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of the force.

Common mix-ups

  • "Each support takes half." Only at the midpoint. Elsewhere the nearer one takes more.
  • "The farther support carries more, since it is farther from the load." The farther one has the longer lever arm, so it needs less force.
  • "A heavier load changes how the weight is shared." It scales both forces and leaves the ratio unchanged.

Things to try on your own

  • Predict NL and NR at x = 4 m, then check.
  • Find the x where the left support carries three times the right.
